title: Analytics / event logging SDK
summary: An SDK used by every feature team to log events: typed schemas, persistent queue, batching and compression, no impact on launch or scroll performance, privacy controls, and guaranteed eventual delivery.
requirements: Simple API: `analytics.track(.screenViewed(name:))`; thread-safe from any context.
No events lost on crash or kill; delivered within minutes; works offline.
Minimal battery, data and launch impact; consent and opt-out respected.
components: Typed event definitions generated from a shared schema registry (also used by Android/backend)
In-memory buffer → append-only on-disk queue (SQLite or segmented files)
Uploader: batches of up to N events or T seconds, gzip, retry with backoff, deletes after 2xx
Context enrichment: session ID, app version, device class, sampling flags
Consent manager and privacy filters; kill switch via remote config
tradeoffs: Writing every event to disk immediately is safest but costs I/O; buffering in memory risks losing the last few events on crash. Common compromise: flush to disk every second and on backgrounding.
Larger batches save radio wake-ups and battery but increase delivery latency.
Typed events catch schema errors at compile time but need codegen and a schema process.
body: **Threading:** public API is nonisolated and cheap (enqueue to an actor or a `Mutex`-protected buffer); all I/O on a background executor; never block the caller.
**Lifecycle:** flush on `didEnterBackground` with `beginBackgroundTask`; schedule `BGAppRefreshTask` for stragglers; upload on next launch after a delay so it does not compete with startup.
**Deduplication:** each event has a UUID; server dedupes retries.
**Queue bounds:** cap disk usage (drop oldest low-priority events first) and record drop counts as a metric.
**Staff angle:** schema governance (owners, review, deprecation), data quality dashboards (events with nulls, volume anomalies), and keeping the SDK's own overhead measured in CI.
